steps.say: The first part of the small bowel can end blind because its channel never hollowed out in the womb. Depending on severity the blockage is a thin membrane, a windsock flap, a fibrous cord or a complete gap. It travels with Down syndrome, twisted midgut, a misplaced portal vein and bile duct atresia.
steps.tx: **Duodenal atresia** (blind duodenum) comes from failed **recanalization** (channel reopening) of the solid cord stage, spanning stenosis, **windsock web** (flap membrane), fibrous cord and complete gap. It associates with prematurity, **Down syndrome** (trisomy 21), **malrotation** (twisted midgut), preduodenal portal vein, **annular pancreas** (ring pancreas) and **biliary atresia** (blocked bile ducts).

steps.say: Bile in the vomit tells you the blockage sits beyond the bile entry point, which is true in the large majority. Scans before birth already flag it, and after birth the plain film shows two bubbles: stomach and duodenum with nothing beyond. A tube down the nose deflates the stomach for the picture.
steps.tx: Obstruction lies distal to the **ampulla of Vater** (bile entry) in **85** (eighty five) percent so infants show **bilious emesis** (bile vomiting), prenatal **ultrasound** (womb scan) detects it, and plain film shows the **double bubble** (twin gas pockets) before tube decompression removes gastric air. The **double bubble** (stomach plus duodenum) with no distal gas is diagnostic.

vis.alt: Supine abdominal X-ray of an infant showing dilated stomach and duodenum, consistent with duodenal atresia.
vis.caption: Double bubble of stomach and duodenum in duodenal atresia. Image: Hellerhoff, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.say: Any gas beyond the two bubbles changes the emergency, demanding a dye study. A twisted midgut can strangle the entire small bowel in hours and outranks the atresia itself. Dye study through the stomach rules the twist in or out, deciding the operation.
steps.tx: Distal air on film mandates **contrast study** (dye swallow) to exclude **malrotation** (unfixed midgut) with **midgut volvulus** (whole-bowel twist), a true surgical emergency that outranks the atresia itself. Missing a volvulus while repairing atresia costs the entire **midgut** (small bowel).

steps.say: The repair joins duodenum to duodenum across the block in a diamond shape that resists narrowing. A hugely stretched upper segment is tapered first, and a web is cut out through the open duodenum with the bile opening carefully preserved. The camera route now handles many cases, shortening recovery. The join must be wide and tension free with the bile opening preserved.
steps.tx: Repair is diamond shaped **duodenoduodenostomy** (duodenum-to-duodenum join), increasingly **laparoscopic** (keyhole), with **tapering duodenoplasty** (narrowing the dilated segment) for a hugely dilated proximal duodenum and transduodenal web excision sparing the **ampulla** (bile opening). The join must be wide and tension free, with the **bile opening** (ampulla) identified and preserved.

steps.say: Further down, a stroke-like accident to the bowel blood supply in the womb seals the gut shut. This commonest gut atresia strikes one in two thousand births with vomiting, swelling and no first stool. One baby in ten hides extra blockages, so salty water is pushed through the far bowel on the table.
steps.tx: **Jejunoileal atresia** (sealed small bowel) is the most common gut atresia at **1** (one) in **2000** (two thousand) births from intrauterine **mesenteric vascular accident** (bowel blood-supply stroke), presenting with bilious vomiting, distention and no **meconium** (first stool), with **10** (ten) to **15** (fifteen) percent multiple atresias needing intraoperative **saline testing** (water flush) of the distal bowel.

steps.say: Five shapes describe the sealed segment from mildest to worst. A membrane, a cord, a V-shaped gap, an apple-peel coil fed backwards by a single fragile vessel, and a string of sausage links. The apple-peel form risks the join failing and leaves dangerously short bowel, and one in ten carries cystic fibrosis.
steps.tx: The five-type **classification** (shape system) runs from web to fibrous cord to V gap to **apple peel atresia** (peel-type IIIb) with retrograde **ileocolic supply** (backwards blood feed) risking anastomotic failure and **short gut** (inadequate length), to string of sausages type IV, and **cystic fibrosis** (thick-secretion disease) affects **10** (ten) percent.

steps.say: Length is the currency of this operation. The surgeon tapers the stretched bowel rather than cutting it away, resects only with plenty to spare, and washes the far end clear. More than nine in ten babies survive to feed normally, thriving thereafter. A stoma is avoided whenever a safe primary join is possible.
steps.tx: Surgery preserves maximal **bowel length** (gut reserve) with **tapering enteroplasty** (narrowing the dilated bowel), resection only with adequate length, and survival exceeds **90** (ninety) percent. Every centimetre saved shortens **parenteral nutrition** (drip feeding) dependence and protects against **short bowel syndrome** (gut failure). Stoma formation is avoided when primary **joining** (direct anastomosis) is safe.

steps.say: The rarest blockage sits in the large bowel, where the film shows stretched featureless loops without the usual pouches. Dye pushed from below confirms the seal, and the repair diverts with an end stoma or joins directly when conditions allow.
steps.tx: **Colonic atresia** (sealed large bowel) is rarest at **5** (five) to **10** (ten) percent of atresias and **1** (one) in **20000** (twenty thousand) births, shows featureless dilated loops without **haustra** (colon pouches), and is confirmed by **contrast enema** (dye from below) with repair by diverting **end colostomy** (stoma) or primary **anastomosis** (direct join).
